description: This bar chart illustrates the number of conversations related to different topics where participants reported being deceived. The horizontal axis represents the categories of conversation topics—Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism—listed in that order from top to bottom. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Conversations,” represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60, with tick marks at 10-unit intervals. For each topic, there are three horizontally arranged bars representing responses to whether participants were “Yes” (red), “Partially” (yellow), or “No” (green) deceived. The “Yes” bar for Journalism is the longest, extending to approximately 52 conversations, while the “Yes” bar for Academic Funding is the shortest, reaching approximately 12 conversations. The “Partially” bars generally range from approximately 10 to 35 conversations, and the “No” bars are consistently the shortest, ranging from approximately 2 to 10 conversations. No bars are visually emphasized, and the bars are not sorted by any apparent criteria. A legend indicates the color coding for each response category.
